process.name: CGS Lead & Opportunity Management (Sales Process)
process.scope: From a team member identifying a lead through to alignment on a discussion document and hand-off into the SOW / proposal process. Proposal drafting, negotiation and effort modelling are a separate documented process.
process.summary: Any CGS team member can identify a lead, which is recorded in Insightly (directly or via an admin). A lead owner runs iterative outreach using sales plays; a response leads to a prepared, transcribed meeting. If an opportunity exists, the lead is converted in Insightly, an opportunity lead is chosen, a team assembled and a discussion document prepared, reviewed where required, and discussed with the prospect. Alignment hands off to proposal development; non-alignment either revises the document or closes the opportunity back to a contact.

roles.name: Lead Identifier (any team member)
roles.description: Any CGS team member who spots a lead from events, news, mergers, tool adoption or visioning work.

roles.name: Director of Operations
roles.description: Confirms lead reassignment; holds an Insightly seat and enters or converts records for team members without access (a delegate may cover).

roles.name: Lead Owner
roles.description: Team member accountable for outreach, meeting scheduling, preparation and the first meeting with the lead.

roles.name: Opportunity Lead
roles.description: Accountable for the opportunity after conversion; assembles the exploration team, prepares and presents the discussion document.

roles.name: Supporting Team Members
roles.description: Provide inputs and existing materials for meeting preparation; may join the opportunity exploration team.

roles.name: Reviewer (Service Line Lead / Leadership)
roles.description: Second pair of eyes on prepared materials and discussion documents, especially where price is referenced.

pain_points.description: Limited Insightly seats mean the 'request assistance' loop recurs at three points (add lead, convert lead, close opportunity).

source_refs.quote: do we also have to do the whole do you have insightly access? ... This is painful.
do we also have to do the whole do you have insightly access?
might not actually have a seat or access edit access

pain_points.description: Team members forget to BCC the Insightly email address; the manual lookup takes 30–60 seconds per email and communications are lost from the record when skipped.

source_refs.quote: every once in a while I forget about it... It's hard to remember when you're doing daily work

pain_points.description: No contact history surfaced at outreach time, so owners may over-contact a lead or pitch a service line the lead already declined.

source_refs.quote: I've sent her now 10 emails in two week increments and she never responded

pain_points.description: No defined criteria for when to cease outreach; it is currently a judgment call. Flagged as an open action item.

source_refs.quote: incorporate a list of reasons we would cease outreach
maybe we reach a point where, okay, we're no longer going to be contacting them

pain_points.description: Contacts that were once leads should still receive periodic nurture (white papers, campaigns) on a priority cadence, but there is no mechanism for this today.

source_refs.quote: you would never turn a lead into a contact and never ever reach out to him or her again

pain_points.description: Lead reassignment decisions tend to escalate to the ELT, pulling leadership into minutia; no sales director role exists to absorb this.

source_refs.quote: if everything goes to the ELT it's kind of the ELT gets into the minutia

pain_points.description: Meeting preparation is frequently skipped or under-done; the team lacks a consistent step for identifying attendees and existing materials.

source_refs.quote: a step that I think we often miss is really prepping for said meeting

pain_points.description: Historically the opportunity meeting was only scheduled after the discussion document was ready, delaying the sales cycle while waiting on the prospect's calendar.

source_refs.quote: we used to schedule the meeting right here and that delays this

pain_points.description: Ownership can become unclear when the lead owner lacks the expertise for the opportunity and wants to hand it to a specialist ('throwing it over the wall').

source_refs.quote: it is not [Lead Owner]'s area of expertise it was actually [service-line lead]

pain_points.description: Review of the discussion document is not formalised; whether a four-eyes review happens depends on who is involved and whether price is mentioned.

source_refs.quote: is a review necessary... depends

open_questions: Define the list of reasons / criteria for ceasing outreach to a lead (action item from workshop).
Confirm who approves lead reassignment when the identifier should not own outreach (Director of Operations vs ELT).
Decide whether the meeting-prep subprocess and the opportunity-lead subprocess should be documented at SOP level.
Confirm the nurture cadence (priority tiers) for leads converted back to contacts.
